This file is where the port is now: a summary checked against the repository, then the
sections that still describe the current design or state, by area. Its history -- the
sections of states since superseded, stage-by-stage logs of finished tracks, the full "Last
updated" list -- is `notes/status-history.md` (append-only). When a section here is superseded,
move it there whole and leave a pointer; the index at the end of this file lists every heading
that moved, so a reference `notes/STATUS.md, "..."` to one of them resolves there. The design
record is `notes/decisions.md`; the Rocq development's notes are on branch `main`
(`git show main:notes/STATUS.md`).

### The closed theorems

Each is about every real execution of a Go program (its package initialization, then `Main`)
from a fresh state with one thread: no thread is stuck, none ended in a panic (so the program's
own check never failed), and the main thread's result, if any, is as stated. The statements and
`#print axioms` are in each `Results.lean`, whose header says more.

- **`k8setcd3_safe`** (`Proof/github_com/mit_pdos/etcd_grove/examples/k8setcd3/Results.lean`,
  from `Adequacy.lean`'s `k8setcd3_adequate`): `examples/k8setcd3` -- one member (the shared
  start), a kubernetes client, two seeded objects in an older encoding, the Kubernetes API server's
  etcd3 store over the client, `clients` clients of `ops` random `Create`/`Get`/`Delete`/
  `GuaranteedUpdate` calls checked by porcupine against the driver's model of the store -- returns
  `Ok` or `Unknown`. Premises: linkvtxn's at the driver's configuration, the Kubernetes packages'
  semantics assumptions (`objTyOk` and `storageErrTyOk` proved from them since 2026-10-27). Rests on three marked
  `sorry`s (`revRoom`, `client_ctx_field`, `kvIs_ne_null`; `clientErr_other` proved 2026-10-26,
  D37b; `notes/k8s-etcd3-plan.md`).
- **`kv_porcupine_safe`** (`Proof/github_com/mit_pdos/etcd_grove/examples/kv/Results.lean`, from
  `AdequacyLinked.lean`'s `kv_adequate`): `examples/kv` -- three raft nodes of a replicated
  key-value store (snapshots and catch-up by `MsgSnap` live since D22 S-r), 4 clients of 25
  random `Put`/`Get`/`Append` on random replicas, porcupine's check -- returns `#()`: porcupine
  always answers `Ok`. Premises: `n < 2^63` steps, the package assumptions, `log.NewModel`. Raft only (no etcd server).
- **`counter_adequate`** (`examples/lintest/counter/Adequacy.lean`; its `Results.lean` restates
  `wp_CheckCounterClock`): porcupine's translated checker accepts the traces of a counter (4
  clients of 10 operations); `n < 2^63`.
- **`logkv_adequate`** (`examples/lintest/logkv/Adequacy.lean`, 2026-10-28): the same for a
  register whose writes go through a log applied by an apply goroutine (`Put` linearizes in the
  apply goroutine: helping through the lock invariant, `notes/logkv-eval.md`); `n < 2^63`.
- **`putget_safe`** (`examples/putget/Results.lean`): one etcd member in process, its gRPC
  server, a client, a `Put` then a `Get` of the key; returns `#()` (the `Get` saw the `Put`).
  Premises (D19a's kinds; `notes/decisions.md`, D19r): the package assumptions (the method-set
  facts are theorems of them since 2026-10-27), `ContextReadErrs` and, since the calls have
  request timeouts (2026-10-23, D-T4), `ContextErrsClient`, the boot facts (`BootFacts`), the
  environment premises `ckptEffectsOk`, `authRecordsFit`, `apply.backendUnderQuota`,
  `storage.dbOpensOk`, unclaimed prometheus names and addresses, `putget.premises`,
  `n + 2 ≤ 2^31`, `n + 7 ≤ backend.wbInit`.
- **`putget3_safe`** (`examples/putget3/Results.lean`): putget's with three members, each serving
  raft on its peer listener; putget's premises for three members.
- **`linkvtxn_safe`** (`examples/linkvtxn/Results.lean`): one member, the robustness tester's KV
  workload (gets, lists, puts, deletes, transactions, compare-and-sets; no leases, no stale
  reads) against the model of etcd's KV; `Ok` or `Unknown`. putget's premises at linkvtxn's
  configuration and `Run`'s bounds on `clients` and `ops`.
- **`linkv3p_safe`** (`examples/linkv3p/Results.lean`): three members whose peer links a schedule
  cuts and mends, and whose client links (through copies of etcd's test bridge) it blackholes,
  unblackholes and drops; three clients each of every member (failover, default retries);
  linkvtxn's workload; `Ok` or `Unknown`, **for every schedule**. putget3's premises, `Run`'s
  bounds, the schedule's length `< 2^63`, `n + 2 ≤ 2^29`.
- **`linkv3p_watch_safe`** (same file): watchkv's workload over the partitioned cluster, a prefix
  watch through the first client, resumed at any member after a cut; result `0`, `1` or `2`
  (`WatchOk`/`WatchFailed`/`WatchEnded`), for every schedule. `linkv3p_safe`'s premises but
  `Run`'s bounds, and watchkv's watcher classes and bounds.
- **`watch_safe`** (`examples/watchkv/Results.lean`): one member, `nw` writers, a prefix watch
  from revision 1; the check that the watched events are exactly the writes (revisions `2, 3,
  ...`, every successful put at its revision) never fails; result `0`, `1` or `2`. putget's
  premises, the client watcher's classes (`ErrorStringNoGRPCStatus`, `ContextErrsClient`, the
  `errors`/`fmt`/`rpctypes` assumptions), `0 ≤ nw < 2^31`, `nw * nops < 2^62`, `n + 2 ≤ 2^29`.
- **`cache_safe`** (`examples/cachekv/Results.lean`): watchkv's program with the watch through
  etcd's `cache` (from revision 2); the same result; `watch_safe`'s premises at cachekv's
  configuration.
- **The witness part**
  (`RaftWitness/Proof/github_com/mit_pdos/etcd_grove/examples/kvwitness/Results.lean`):
  `kv_porcupine_safe` (the kv example on the witness raft) and **`kv_witness_porcupine_safe`**
  (`MainWitness`: two voters and an in-process witness, raft's static mode); kv's premises.
  `RaftWitness/Proof/go_etcd_io/raft/v3/Results.lean` restates no theorem (`#print axioms` of
  the linked results).

Retired (2026-10-22, `notes/decisions.md` D34): **`linkv_safe`** (`examples/linkv`: one member,
`lintest.Run` of random Puts and Gets against a values-only key-value model) and **`linkv3_safe`**
(`examples/linkv3`: linkv's workload over three members, a client to the first), subsumed by
`linkvtxn_safe` (Puts, Gets, Deletes, Txns against etcd's KV model, on the same axioms) and
`linkv3p_safe` (three members, every client of every member, any partition schedule). Their
sections are in `notes/status-history.md` ("D20 (c): linked, initialized, closed", "D20: linkv3,
the three-member instance" and their earlier stages); what linkvtxn and linkv3p took from linkv
moved to them (D34).

Raft's own results are `Proof/go_etcd_io/raft/v3/Results.lean` (the model-level safety lemmas no
linked result used were removed on 2026-10-21: "Clean-up: unused declarations removed, ..."
below).

## Perennial pin `6da88b280` (2026-10-30, branch `pin-6da88b2`)

The pin `ad74ee4f6` -> `6da88b280` (Perennial `lean`, 54 commits), for `wp_slice_literal_nonnull`
(G2's watch: an empty slice literal is not `nil`; `notes/perennial-changes.md`, "Slices: an empty
slice literal is not nil"). It also brings the Go-semantics changes R1/R2/R5 (integers and floats
are little-endian bytes, integer atomics are byte atomics), plain types with gc's layout at positive
addresses, a heap bounded below 2^47, R3 (unsafe conversions, `uintptr`, `unsafe.Add`/`Slice`),
goose's slice of a pointer to an array, and `sync.Pool`'s trusted `Get`/`Put`.

- **Translations.** `etc/goose.py` with the new translator: no file changed in any project
  (`--check` passes); `etc/gen-init.py --check`: 199 files up to date.
- **What broke**: one cause, four lemmas. A `w64`'s typed points-to is now its 8 bytes
  (`bytesTypedPointsto 8`), not a heap points-to of the value, so `typedPointstoDef_heap` no longer
  rewrites it. The lemmas that two whole `w64` points-tos (or a whole and a part) contradict now
  unfold to the bytes (`simp only [typedPointstoDef_w64, natBytes, bytesPointsto]`) and combine the
  first byte's heap points-tos: `w64Field_excl` (`lease/LessorLemmas`), `w64_ptsto_excl`
  (`cache/v3/InvEtcdTxn`), `ptsto_w64_valid` (`client/v3/WatchRecon`), `mv_w64_excl`
  (`mvcc/MoveVictimsLemmas`). Nothing else: the atomics this repository uses directly are on
  `Bool` (`wp_cmpxchg_suc`), whose instances stayed; Perennial's own `sync/atomic` proofs moved to
  the byte atomics behind unchanged specs. No statement changed.
- **Checks.** Full `lake build` green; `etc/tcb-report.py --check` and every collection match
  (766 axioms, 25 `sorry`s: no change); `etc/api-check.py` and `etc/gen-interface.py --check
  --layout` on `etc/api/raft.txt` pass (no interface change). `etc/gen-link.py`: every mode matches
  its `Link.lean` but six whose differences predate the bump (the script reads nothing of
  Perennial): `--mvcc`, `--txn`, `--apply`, `--read` (the committed files have a `variable [raftAsm
  : go_etcd_io.raft.v3.Assumptions]` the script does not emit) and `--lintest-logkvcompact`,
  `--lintest-logkvsnap` (a docstring wording).
- **Tooling note.** `etc/lean-check.py` with `LAKE_OPTS=--packages=<path manifest>` does not work:
  the server's `lake setup-file` does not get the option and tries to check the pin out in the
  shared `.lake/packages/perennial` (it failed, nothing changed); use `lake build --packages=...`
  on the modules instead.

## Two compaction-path axioms refuted (2026-10-29)

The `axiom` skill, run from the backend-compaction stage (`backend-cmp`):
- **`mvcc.kbNoCmp_metaNone` is false** (`notes/axiom-review/nocmpread.md`; counterexample on branch
  `axiom/kbnocmp-metanone`). Its premise does not tie the reader to the backend, so one backend's
  no-compaction token says every reader finds no compaction, for good. Go finds one after the
  store compacts. Its two uses (`store.restore`) are true instances; 21 exported results rest on it.
  **Not fixed on `lean`:** the fix is the compaction keys' tracked absence in the backend model
  (the axiom deleted, `backend-cmp` `2e49ff1aa9`), which comes with a merge of `backend-cmp`.
- **`storage.OpenBackend` is false as documented** (`notes/axiom-review/openbackend.md`;
  counterexample on branch `axiom/openbackend`). A `QuotaBackendBytes` whose 110% exceeds bbolt's
  `MaxMapSize` makes `newBackend` panic in any environment. **Fixed:** `openPre` takes
  `openMmapOk cfg`, a new pure premise of `NewServer.spec`/`specCompact`/`specM` and passed through
  D22's `applySnapshot.specSnap`/`applySnapshot_walk`/`srvSnapRO`. The examples discharge it (quota 0).
  The etcd side is in `issues/etcd-quota-backend-bytes-mmap-panic.md`.

## Two bbolt axioms refuted (2026-10-29, on `lean`)

The `axiom` skill's review of the bbolt axioms (`notes/axiom-review/bbolt.md`): **`backend.ownWTxG_fill`
is false**, with a counterexample proved: `examples/axiomcx/bboltnan`'s `Run` sets a bucket's
`FillPercent` to NaN, puts 70000 keys and commits; the axioms prove it returns
(`Proof/.../examples/axiomcx/bboltnan/Run.lean`, no `sorry`), Go panics in `Commit`
(`inode overflow`, amd64; `issues/bbolt-fillpercent-nan.md`). **`bbolt.Bucket.Put_kv` is false**
too (with `Commit_kv` and the cursor specs), by two earlier `issues/` reproductions
(`bbolt-max-value-size-unusable`, `bbolt-large-values-leaf-unreadable`) not yet reflected in the
axiom. Neither reaches etcd (it writes `FillPercent = 0.9` and bounds requests at 1.5 MiB), but
every result through the backend's writes rests on both. Not fixed: the report proposes
restatements, awaiting a decision. The rest survived the attacks listed there, including a
differential fuzzer (`etc/spec-test/bbolt-diff`, 24000 runs). `notes/audit.md`'s two rows updated.

## The informers, fifth round: the reflector's list-watch (2026-10-28, branch `k8s-daemonset-proof`)

Phase 4's fifth round (`notes/k8s-daemonset-plan.md`, phase 4, "fifth round"), under D51 (no new
axioms; a gap or an unapproved boundary callee is a named hypothesis, `?` in
`etc/link-lean-first-k8scache.txt`, so `section links_pending` of the cache's `Link.lean`).

- **The reflector's state** (`RefInf.lean`): `reflSt r γa γi n`, the reflector goroutine's fields
  (`reflOwn`: last synced version, "unavailable" flag; `reflMisc`: `paginatedResult`, the watch
  timeouts), the invariant's half of its last version `n`, and a past API state at least `n` (so a
  relist is at least it). The list-watcher's contract `lwOk` (the model's typed `List`/`Watch` of
  the informer's resource: a `List` of a state at least any the caller knew; `typedListAt` now
  says a list has no continue token, apimodel's proof layer only).
- **Proved** (Spec + Proof, linked): `Reflector.list` (the listing goroutine with its `recover`,
  the pager at `relistResourceVersion()` and the retry from `""` after an expired or too-large
  version, the wait on the context, `syncWith`'s `Replace` pushed through `infInv_pushReplaceAU`:
  the list's objects registered, the log's table at a version at least the reflector's last),
  `Reflector.watch` (the watch loop from the last version: every event through `watch_evStepOk`, a
  change the log's next, a bookmark quiet; backoff after a retriable error, return after any
  other), `handleWatch`, `watchWithResync` (the resync goroutine under a child context,
  Perennial's `WithCancel`; its error channel never sent on), `startResync`/`resyncChan` (resync
  period `0`, `Main`'s), `ListAndWatchWithContext` (watch-list off: from `reflSt n`, it returns at
  some version `k`, at `n` after a failed list, or with the context seen done: `lwPost`), the
  pager (`New`, `SimplePageFunc`, `ListPager.list`, `ListWithAlloc`), `isExpiredError`,
  `isWatchErrorRetriable`, `isUnsupportedTableListObject`, `NewRetryWithDeadline`,
  `retryWithDeadlineImpl.reset`/`ShouldRetry`. Context facts in `RefCtx.lean` (`stableCtx`: a
  context whose `Done` is a fixed channel, `ctxSeen` once a receive on it succeeded).
- **Named hypotheses** (`?`): gaps `handleAnyWatch` (D4, `notes/k8s-daemonset-goose.md`) and
  `retryWithDeadlineImpl.After` (Perennial's `time` lacks `Time.IsZero`,
  `notes/perennial-changes.md`); not proved this round, `isTooLargeResourceVersionError` (needs
  `APIStatus`'s assertion and method specs); **pending approval** (boundary callees), the
  `apierrors` predicates (`IsResourceExpired`, `IsGone`, `IsTooManyRequests`, `IsInternalError`),
  `meta.ListAccessor`/`ExtractListWithAlloc`/`LenList`, `Trace.Step`; outside client-go, names
  only: klog's `FromContext` (non-nil context), logr's `V`/`Info`, `utilnet.IsConnectionRefused`,
  `rand.Float64`, `RealClock.After`, `wait.Group.Start`. Premises (not axioms): `rvuTyOk`, `bmTyOk`
  (`*RealFIFO`'s method sets), `errIsOk`, `Float64ToInt64Semantics` (the watch timeout).
- **Trust base unchanged**: the new results use only existing axioms (`RealClock.Now`,
  `Duration.Seconds_ptr`, `trace.New`/`LogIfLong`, `fmt.Errorf`) and the two `reflect.Type'`
  instance `sorry`s of the fourth round (the `Reflector` struct); `etc/tcb-report.py --check`
  matches `etc/tcb-baseline.txt` (751 axioms, 11 sorries). `meta.List`/`meta.Type` are now
  translated interface types (`meta.toml` imports `metav1`), not axiomatized types.
  `#print axioms` in `Proof/k8s_io/client_go/tools/cache/Results.lean`.
- **`HasSynced` ⇒ the first list is in the store** (`InformerSync.lean`, `InformerHasSynced.lean`;
  proved, no axiom). The invariant `infRes` gains the first list's version `f` (ghost `γi.first`,
  persistent once set: `infFirst γi v`) and the pure `syncOk`: before the first list the FIFO is
  empty, nothing is popped, the reflector has no version; after it, the FIFO's
  `initialPopulationCount` is the position of the first relist's delta among the deltas not yet
  done (after the applied-not-done ones, `apN`), or the store is already at its version; once
  synced, the store's version is at least `v`. Every accessor re-proved (`sync_pop`, `sync_apply`,
  `sync_done`, `sync_push`, `sync_replace_first`). New accessors: `infInv_hasSyncedAU` (at
  `HasSynced`'s linearization point, `true` gives `infFirst γi v ∗ infRvLb γi v`),
  `infInv_readLbAU` (a later store read is the server's table at a version at least such a bound);
  `infInv_pushReplaceAU` now also gives the reflector `infFirst` at its first list (`firstIf`).
  Linked: `RealFIFO_HasSynced_inf` (`Results.lean`). Not yet threaded: the first list's version
  against the state `Main` knew when it started the informer (the reflector's `list` gets a state
  at least it; `lwPost` does not carry `infFirst` out), and the informer's own `HasSynced` chain
  (`sharedIndexInformer` → `controller` → the FIFO, and C2's forwards).
  An observation, not reachable from the reflector: Go's `Pop`/`PopBatch` lower the count for a
  delta popped before the first `Replace` (a bookmark, which does not populate the queue) when its
  processing ends after that `Replace`, so a FIFO fed a bookmark first could report synced before
  the relist is processed; `syncOk`'s "empty before the first list" is what excludes it (the
  reflector lists first).
- **Not done this round**: `RunWithContext` (needs `wait`'s backoff `Until` and the watch error
  handler as hypotheses), the handlers' order against the chain (the handler history `γe` is not
  yet tied to the applied deltas), and the construction and `Run` of `Main`'s four informers
  (blocked on D2/C2).

## The informers, fourth round: the batch path, the reflector, the contract (2026-10-27, branch `k8s-daemonset-proof`)

Phase 4's fourth round (`notes/k8s-daemonset-plan.md`, phase 4, "fourth round"), under D51: `Main`
keeps `InOrderInformersBatchProcess` on, so the informers take the batch path.

- **The batch path, over two named hypotheses** (`BatchDefs.lean`; `?` in
  `etc/link-lean-first-k8scache.txt`, so `section links_pending` of `Link.lean`):
  `threadSafeMap.Transaction` (gap C4: the store after `St.txn`, each key's last write, the
  resource version the last object's when it has one) and `RealFIFO.PopBatch` (gap D3: the batch
  `FQ.batch`, `Pop`'s two linearization points, the deferred `FQ.popDoneN`, a lone delta by the
  single processing function). Both stated as what the code does (read 2026-10-27; reviewed by a
  fresh agent against the Go: no soundness problem; its one finding, that `popDoneN`'s `Nat`
  count cannot follow Go's `initialPopulationCount` below zero, is now a premise the caller shows
  at the deferred step, true of the informer's queue). **Proved over them**: `cache.Transaction`,
  `processDeltasInBatch` (the loop's writes `batchTxs`, the callbacks as closures over their
  iteration's `old`/`obj` made read-only, `inBatch`, one `Transaction`, the callbacks in order:
  `batchStep`), the shared informer's `handleBatchDeltas`, and `controller.processLoop` on **both**
  paths (the gate now returns any boolean, `gateOk`; the single-delta proof kept, the processing's
  contracts one family over batches). New method-set premise `batchTyOk` (`methodSet` is
  uninterpreted: `*threadSafeMap`, `*cache`, `*RealFIFO` implement the batch interfaces).
- **The store writer's allowed steps** (`InformerDefs.lean`): `storeWriter γ SW Rw` now admits only
  the steps `Rw σ σ'` (reads, and the delta's own store step `storeStepFD`/`batchStore`, both
  idempotent); every processing spec takes `⌜Rw σ σ ∧ Rw σ (step)⌝`. Why: the informer contract
  keeps the store's state in an invariant its readers (the listers) open, which cannot admit an
  arbitrary write; the old `storeWriter` (any `σ'`) made that impossible. Re-proved: `processDeltas`,
  `processReplacedAllInfo`, `reconcileReplacement`, `handleDeltas`, the batch path.
- **The reflector, first functions** (`RefDefs.lean`: the last synced version and the "unavailable"
  flag, owned by the reflector's goroutine, the only one that reads them in `Main`):
  `LastSyncResourceVersion`, `setLastSyncResourceVersion`, `setIsLastSyncResourceVersionUnavailable`,
  `relistResourceVersion` (`relistRV`), `rewatchResourceVersion`, `syncWith` (logically atomic at the
  FIFO's `Replace`).
- **Trust base**: new boundary axiom `errors.Join.wp_proof` (Go's "Join returns nil if every value
  is nil"); the two named hypotheses are not axioms but hypotheses of the results that reach them.
  **Two new `sorry`s** reached by the reflector's proofs: `reflect.Type'`'s generated instances
  (`Type'_typed_pointsto`, `Type'_into_val_typed`): `reflect` is names-only in Perennial and the
  `Reflector` struct has a `reflect.Type` field, so its instances rest on them
  (`notes/perennial-changes.md`, "`reflect.Type` in a struct field"). Baselines updated deliberately
  (`etc/tcb-baseline.txt`, `clientgo-cache`, `clientgo-informers`).
- **The informer contract, started** (`InformerContract.lean`, `InformerRel.lean`,
  `InformerInv.lean`, `InformerGlue.lean`; all proved, no axiom, no `sorry`, checked with
  `#print axioms`). The model: an informer's state `InfP` (the store's view, the popped deltas, the
  queue, the reflector's last version) is **a chain over the server's log** (`InfP.ok`, from
  `InformerModel.lean`): the store is the log's table at its version, each queued delta is the next
  change after the previous version, a bookmark with no change between, or a relist at a version at
  least the last; so versions never decrease (`apply_rv_le`) and the store is the API state at its
  version (`ok_store`). The invariant `infInv γa r γf γt γi` (one per informer, namespace `infN`)
  ties it to the Go state: a past API state `σp` (`pastSt`), a registry of the Go objects handed to
  the FIFO with their model objects (ghost map, each object read-only: `objAt … discard`, deep
  persistence for every API type, `Proof/k8s_io/api/DeepBase.lean` and the generator
  `etc/gen-k8s-deep.py`), the FIFO's and the store's client halves, the processing goroutine's
  popped batch, the reflector's last version, a monotone lower bound on the store's version (what a
  lister reader keeps), and the pure relations (`fdRel`, `storeRel`, `poppedRel`, `fqOk`, keys
  good). **Accessors proved through it**: a lister read (`infInv_readAU`: the store's items are the
  log's table at a version at least every earlier read's), `PopBatch`/`Pop` and the deferred step
  (`infInv_popBatchAU`, `infInv_doneBatchAU`), the store writers of a batch and of one delta with
  their allowed steps (`infInv_batchWriter`, `infInv_singleWriter`, `…Finish`), registering an
  object (`infInv_register`), and the reflector's three pushes, each from **any** past state the
  reflector saw (ordered with the invariant's by `pastSt_cmp`): a watch change that is the log's
  next after its last version (`infInv_pushChangeAU`), a quiet bookmark (`infInv_pushBookmarkAU`),
  a relist's `Replace` of the log's table at the list's version, at least its last
  (`infInv_pushReplaceAU`). Phase D uses `infInv` and these accessors as the informers' contract.
- **A change to the apimodel's proof layer** (not its Go): `pastSt` now carries `histOk` of its
  history (`Defs.lean`), so two past states are ordered (`HistLemmas.lean`: `pairwise_cmp`,
  `pastSt_cmp`); `pastSt_of_auth` re-proved, every apimodel and dsmain proof re-checked.
- **Not done in this round**: the reflector's `list` (pager, the goroutine with `recover`, boundary
  axioms needed for `meta.ListAccessor`, `ExtractListWithAlloc`, `LenList`, `Trace.Step` and the
  `apierrors` predicates), `watch`, `ListAndWatchWithContext`, `watchWithResync`/`startResync`;
  `handleAnyWatch`'s hypothesis spec (D4) not yet written; the informer's construction and
  `RunWithContext`; the `HasSynced` part of the contract (synced only after the first relist is in
  the store: needs the first `Replace`'s position against `initCount` in the invariant); the
  handlers' part (each handler sees the store's changes in order: relating the notification history
  `γe` to the chain); typed informers (D2/C2).

## The informers, third round: index values per item (2026-10-27, branch `k8s-daemonset-proof`)

Phase 4's third round (`notes/k8s-daemonset-plan.md`, phase 4, "third round"). **Index values per
item** (the approved design change): an index function's contract is now a relation between an
object and its values (`StoreDefs.lean`'s `Fn GF := GoInterface → List GoString → IProp GF`,
functional, `fnFun`), no longer a pure function of the interface value (which cannot describe a
heap-allocated object's fields). The store's lock invariant records each item's values per indexer
(`StoreModel.lean`'s `IV`, `tsP`'s `iv`, `itemsIv`), exact for the indices (`ixOk`) and none for
absent or `nil` items or non-indexers (`ivWf`); the abstract state `St` and every writer's spec are
unchanged. The index queries return the relation's facts: `ByIndex`/`Index` (and
`ListAllByNamespace`'s `nsKeys`, the listers' `List`) give `idxSel F items S ks`: the keys whose
recorded values meet `S`, with `F o vs` for each item (so a client whose relation reads the
namespace learns each returned object's namespace); `Index` also the query object's values `vq`.
Re-proved: `updateSingleIndex`, `updateIndices` (now: the key's new values `vs`, the old ones under
other names), `updateLocked`/`deleteLocked` (now return the whole invariant), `Update`,
`DeleteWithObject`, `Replace`, `AddIndexers` (the re-indexing loop over recorded values),
`ByIndex`, `Index`, `getKeysFromIndex`, `NewThreadSafeStore`, `ListAllByNamespace`, the listers. No
axiom or `sorry` added (`etc/tcb-report.py --check` and both client-go collections unchanged).

## client-go's consistency store verified (2026-10-27, branch `k8s-leaf-cache`)

Phase 2 of the DaemonSet plan, its `util/consistency` part (`notes/k8s-daemonset-plan.md`, phase 2's
status): `etc/gen-link.py --consistency` links `Proof/k8s_io/client_go/util/consistency/` (with
apimachinery's `resourceversion`) in its `Link.lean`; results in `Results.lean`, TCB
`etc/tcb-collections/clientgo-consistency.txt`. Every translated function of the package is proved,
no `sorry`. `WroteAt`, `Clear` and `EnsureReady` are logically atomic (`<<{ … }>>`, AtomicFupd)
over the abstract state `consState γ M` (`M`: owner to UID and newest version per group resource;
`Model.lean`), linearizable although `WroteAt` writes the record after finding it and
`EnsureReady` clears it in a second critical section: the invariant (`Defs.lean`, `consInv`) tracks
pending writes (the abstract versions are the newest of the physical and pending ones,
`absVsOk`) and `EnsureReady`'s slot (it deposits its permission, and deletes the record abstractly
when the check passes). The documented precondition ("Must not be called concurrently with WroteAt
for the same owner") is a resource: the store is built for caller-chosen fractional permissions
`T o q` (`WroteAt` needs some `T o q`, `EnsureReady` `T o 1`, `tokExcl T`). `EnsureReady` returns
`nil` only with `readyRec`: per recorded version, a registered store returned a non-empty `readRV`
with the caller's contract `G` and, if `readRV` is well formed, at least the recorded one (the
fail-open on a malformed `readRV`, `"0"`, stated; judged unreachable over kube-apiserver,
`issues/nonissues/k8s-consistency-malformed-rv-ready.md`). `LastSyncRVGetter` is an abstract
contract (`getterOk`). Trust boundary: `resourceversion.isWellFormed` (gap C1) and
`schema.GroupResource.String` (names only), both axioms; `CompareResourceVersion` proved as the
comparison of decimal values (`lexCmp_eq_cmpNat`). Callers need one of the map lock's reader slots
per concurrent `WroteAt`/`EnsureReady` (`consReader`, `NewConsistencyStore` hands out all).
Tooling note: `wp_apply` misbehaves after an atomic spec applied with `iapply`
(`notes/perennial-changes.md`).

## A durable kv example and the durable-state extension (2026-10-27, branch `worktree-durable-kv`)

Nothing proved (the raft proof is being refactored); the code, its GooseLang extension and its
translation are in place for proofs later.

- **`examples/durable`**: a node's durable state, named files read and written whole
  (`Read(name) (string, bool)`, `Write(name, data)`): the operating system's file API only
  (`os.ReadFile`; a temporary file, synced, renamed over the file, the directory synced), the
  operations serialized and retried until they succeed. Its functions are `trusted`
  (`Code/github_com/mit_pdos/etcd_grove/examples/durable.toml`), modeled by
  `TrustedCode/github_com/mit_pdos/etcd_grove/examples/durable.lean`.
- **The extension `durableExt`** (`GooseLang/Ext/Durable/Impl.lean`, trusted: the operations
  `"Read"`/`"Write"` on a map from names to contents, absent files included; files survive a
  crash) and `Specs.lean` (proved, no `sorry`): the ghost state is one ghost variable of all
  the files (`durableOwn fs`, so a spec can say a file is absent), `wp_DurableRead`,
  `wp_DurableWrite` and their logically atomic forms, and a closed program proving
  `HasExt durableExt` by `rfl`. The proof prelude `Proof/DurablePrelude` (lakefile glob
  `GooseLang.+`). No crash adequacy instance yet (Perennial's `fsExt` has one,
  `Perennial/GooseLang/Ext/Fs/Adequacy.lean`).
- **`examples/durablekv`**: kv (Put, Get, Append through the log) with each replica's raft
  state -- hard state, log, latest snapshot (which holds the store and the answers of the
  operations applied) -- in one file, rewritten whole before a Ready's messages are sent and
  after each snapshot and compaction (every 100 entries); a replica restarts from its file
  (`raft.RestartNode`, `Applied` at the snapshot) and replays its log. Clients (`Cluster`) give
  operations unique encodings (an epoch kept durably in `dir/epoch`, a sequence number) and
  propose one again, with the same encoding, after a crash or a timeout; a repeat is answered
  with the recorded answer. Tests (`go test ./durablekv`, race-clean): porcupine with random
  replicas crashing and restarting, the whole cluster stopped and restarted past several
  snapshots, the storage's encoding round trip; `cmd/durablekv` runs the check and `put`/`get`
  across processes. Porcupine's search, not the store, keeps the check to about 8 clients.
- **Translation**: projects `durable` and `durablekv` of `etc/goose.py`; goose needs to know
  nothing of the extension (the trusted model names it). The pin `25bd32450` (Perennial's
  extensions named in the syntax: `notes/perennial-changes.md`, "GooseLang: extensions outside
  Perennial, named in the syntax", landed) has the Perennial side; the bump from `edcadb1e5`
  changed no translation but `durablekv`'s.

## kvreconf's snapshot goroutine (2026-10-30, branch `repair`)

kvreconf's snapshots and compaction are in a goroutine of their own per replica (`snapshotter`; `run`
sends it requests on a capacity-1 channel without waiting), as etcd's apply thread does beside the
raft goroutine (`notes/decisions.md`, "kvreconf's snapshots in a goroutine of their own").
`MemoryStorage`'s specs are the two-writer ones the server's repair will reuse: the persistent
`memSnapLb γs i` in place of the exclusive `memSnapExact` (`CreateSnapshot` either way, `Compact`,
`ApplySnapshot`), `NewMemoryStorage`'s exclusive `memSnapNone` (opened by `memSnapNone_open`), and
`Snapshot`'s `b = true` form answering exactly the empty snapshot while `memSnapNone` is held (R1).
The deviations and the server's note: `notes/raft-unified-plan.md`, "Spec changes during U8 v2",
the kvreconf-snapshot-thread entry. Raft's MemoryStorage proofs and kvreconf's (`request`,
`snapshot`, `snapshotter`, `run`, `stop`, `newReplica`; `maybeSnapshot`/`maybeCompact` removed)
re-proved, `kvreconf_porcupine_safe` rebuilt with the same statement, no `sorry`, no new axiom.
A local Perennial-shaped lemma: `bag_nb_send_au` (`notes/perennial-changes.md`).

## Raft unified, stages U2, U3 (done): snapshots in the dynamic mode (2026-10-28, branch `raft-unified`)

U2: the dynamic snapshot certificate is made and read. Raft's names may name a registry of the
snapshots the application made (`RaftNames.reSnapReg`, `none` in every allocation until U4); a
snapshot's data certificate carries its key there (`snapRegOk`), and raft's configuration
certificate says it is at a committed prefix of its length and last term whose fold is its
configuration (`snapAtOk`). `Protocol/SnapCertDyn.lean`: `raftSnapCert_make_dyn` (a committed prefix
is the only full log with records ending at its id). `SnapsMade.lean` (internal, `ApiImpl`):
`ownSnapsMade`/`snapMade`/`snapMade_elem`, `snapshotCert_make`, `snapshotCert_made` over
`RuleNames γ r c0` (the rule and `c0` explicit until U9). Two departures from candidate 12 (a fancy
update; a `SnapListsOk` premise, kept by decision, with derivation laws for clients still to state).

U3a (the model) and U3b (`raft.Step`) done: a restore keeps the configuration index (its prefix
extends the node's committed prefix, from the message's commit fact), so the configuration is the
fold of the full log's prefix also with a snapshot pending (`RInv.cfg` unconditional); conf changes
and apply acknowledgements of a `Ready` handed out before a restore go on with the snapshot pending
(`applyConf`, `advance`); `applySnap` applies a snapshot at or below the boundary (the pending one or
an older one), moving the configuration index there. `raft.Step`'s snapshot acknowledgement is proved
in the dynamic mode too (premise `SnapAckDyn`; `GMove`'s fourth case), and its `MsgStorageApplyResp`
no longer needs no snapshot pending.

U3c done: the dynamic `RawNode` takes, hands out and acknowledges snapshots. `DynNoSnap` is gone
(`RawNode.Step` takes a `MsgSnap` in either mode; `raft.Step` no longer takes `GMode.SnapDyn`: the
dynamic mode's need is the message's certificate, and `StepCDS` asks a snapshot's admissibility only
when its lists name the node); `"%Hsnap"` holds in either mode; `Advance` of a dynamic snapshot `Ready`
supplies `SnapAckDyn` from the certificate at the loan's committed log and moves the configuration
index and configuration to the snapshot's (`advRS`, `RNMode.foldCfg`); it takes the snapshot's
`ConfState` not auto-leave (dynamically, until U5). No new `sorry` or axiom; no exported
statement moved. `notes/decisions.md`, "Stages U2, U3".

U3d done: the node layer takes snapshots in the dynamic mode (`runCfg`, `readySnapData`: a node that
takes `MsgSnap`s is outside the no-snapshot mode, in either mode). The driver's view of the
configuration moves at the `advancec` rendezvous after a snapshot `Ready` (its half in the payload,
back at the snapshot's index and the fold of its committed log, `loanCfg`/`capPay`/`capAns`; `run`
holds `runCfgR` until `RawNode.Advance`). A conf change applied while a snapshot `Ready` is lent (an
entry of the loan's committed log) is supported (`wp_applyConf_dyn` over `rsDlv`). The API's
`nodeDriver` carries the storage's certificate link in a dynamic cluster outside the no-snapshot mode,
and `hsCommitted` says nothing there. `node.Advance.dynamicSpec`'s post (approved): after a snapshot
`Ready`, `∃ m, nodeConfig ⟨index, m⟩ ∗ ⌜confStateIs cs m⌝`, vacuous today (dynamic clusters are in the
no-snapshot mode). No new `sorry` or axiom. `notes/decisions.md`, "Stage U3d". U4 not started (2026-10-28: the user
replaced the fixed `ConfRule` by a TaDa per-entry decision; U4's allocation waits for that design).

## `examples/kvreconf`: snapshots and reconfiguration together, Go only (2026-10-28, branch `kv-snap-reconf`)

A key-value store on `raft.Node` whose test program is meant as a specification of how an
application may use raft (the package's comment): every choice the application may make is made at
random (`primitive.RandomUint64`), so that its executions cover the interleavings of requests with
snapshots and configuration changes. The target of the unified proof (D1 below: the proofs' modes
take snapshots or reconfiguration, not both).

- bootstrap by `StartNode` (1 to 5 voters); newcomers by `RestartNode` on an empty `MemoryStorage`;
  removed replicas keep running (they may be added back with their old log); raft's options random
  (`PreVote`, `CheckQuorum`, `StepDownOnRemoval`, message and inflight limits, tick rates);
- snapshots after any applied entry (mid-Ready) or Ready, compaction to any allowed index, a
  storage that may answer `ErrSnapshotTemporarilyUnavailable`;
- one to three proposers of random conf changes at random times through random replicas (simple
  and joint, `ConfChange`/`ConfChangeV2`, every transition, explicit leaves, junk), unserialized; a
  replica applies a committed change only if raft's `confchange` accepts it on its configuration
  (`validConf`), and otherwise rejects it by not calling `ApplyConfChange`;
- the network drops, duplicates, delays and reorders; random transfers, `Campaign`,
  `ForgetLeader`, `ReportSnapshot` outcomes;
- clients: Put and Get through the log, Read by `ReadIndex`, retried at random members with the
  same operation id.

`kvreconf.Main`: runs it and panics unless porcupine answers Ok (the adequacy target);
`TestRounds` and `go run ./cmd/kvreconfcheck -rounds N` also check convergence and coverage. Not
durable: `MemoryStorage`, no crash or restart (the user's scope).

Found while writing it:

- [issues/raft-snapshot-during-apply-stale-confchange](../issues/raft-snapshot-during-apply-stale-confchange.md)
  reached in a full cluster: raft panics in `applyConfChange` (1 of 17 rounds on the pinned raft).
  With the issue's fix ported to the fork (`issues/raft-conf-lag-model/fork-v3.7-applied-snap-config.patch`,
  `patch -p1` on `raft37-goose-lean-a1`; raft's tests and the fix's regression test pass), 15 rounds
  passed. A local fork branch, `raft37-goose-lean-a2` (`565c2bd`, on `c8217eb9`), in a checkout
  at `.lake/raft-fork` of the worktree (not pushed; the patch is its `format-patch`); the raft pin is
  unchanged (`etc/goose.py --src raft=.lake/raft-fork` translates from it).
- [issues/raft-snapshot-without-recipient-livelock](../issues/raft-snapshot-without-recipient-livelock.md):
  a newcomer added after the storage's latest snapshot is sent it forever once the log is
  compacted (with random snapshots, a later one ends it).
- Stopping a removed voter as soon as some replica applied its removal can leave the remaining
  voter, which has not applied it, needing its vote forever (why removed replicas keep running).
- `examples/kv`'s transport steps a forwarded `MsgProp` with `context.Background()`; `Node.Step` of
  a `MsgProp` blocks while the target knows no leader, which in `kvreconf` blocked a candidate's
  loop before it handled the Ready persisting its own vote (fixed there with a 5ms step timeout).
  `kv`'s is the same pattern (partial correctness: a hang is no violation; not observed).
- `MaxSizePerMsg: 0` with `MaxCommittedSizePerReady: 0` panics
  (`issues/nonissues/raft-zero-max-size-per-msg.md`); the random options avoid the pair.

## The key-value store on the implemented node API (2026-10-27, branch `kv-port`)

with no `sorry`). `lake build ...kv.Results ...kv.AdequacyLinked` is green and no kv result reaches a
`sorry` (`kv_adequate`, `kv_Put`, ..., `kv_Main`: none).

- `KV.Read`: `Draft.readStateOk_ctx` as proved (a ghost update, given the applier's committed log
  `ap` at least `i` long; two later credits from `wp_auto_lc 2` strip `▷ ▷`).
- `run` applies committed conf changes again, as the Go code does: a type-`1` committed entry is a
  requested one (never a filler), so in `ops` (`ownCommittedOps_lb_prefix`), whose conf changes are
  `RemoveMember`'s (`kvCore`'s new `RmReqs`, `kv_committed_cc`); its bytes decode (`proto.Unmarshal`)
  to `rmCC id` and `node.ApplyConfChange` takes it (static cluster, `CCShrink`); `reconf` is set and
  no more snapshots are taken. `isStaticCluster_normal` (false) is gone, and kv needs no filler law.
- **`KV.RemoveMember` takes a premise, `RmShrink id`**: the change it proposes is a `CCShrink` of
  `kvVoters` (it keeps the voters, dropping at most a learner), i.e. `id` is not a voter. Raft's API
  covers `ApplyConfChange` only for such changes in a static cluster; the premise is unsatisfiable
  for a voter, which is what `RemoveMember` is for in Go (`TestRemoveMember` removes replica 3), the
  way the earlier proof's `CCAllowed` premise was in the static cluster. Removing a voter needs a
  dynamic `ApplyConfChange` in the node API. `kv_ccAu` takes it, `RmReqs` carries it.

## The node API over an abstract log, implemented (2026-10-27, branch `raft-api`)

`Proof/go_etcd_io/raft/v3/NodeApiImpl.lean` (namespace `ApiImpl`) implements the API
(`NodeApiDraft.lean`) over raft's internals; the draft's predicates are sealed over it and every law
and spec of the draft is proved (no `sorry` left in the draft; `#print axioms` of its specs: raft's
existing trust-boundary axioms only). Its pure vocabulary is `NodeApiVocab.lean` (with `strip`, a raft
log as the client sees it).

- **Ghost state** (`Cluster`): raft's names, two monotone lists of `LogEntry` (`full`, the committed
  log; `ops`, its requested entries, halved between the client and the adapter), the read contexts
  (`ctxs`, ghost map `c ↦ γq`), the cluster's term budget, the trivial predicate's name (`trueQ`).
  The adapter's invariant `apiInv` (at `N .@ "api"`; raft's commit invariant at `N .@ "raft"`) holds
  raft's client half `rLog`, the authorities, and the fresh-token authorities with what the adapter
  registered and deposited. `isCommittedLogLb` is `l = []` or the two lower bounds.
- **Every cluster is static and takes snapshots** (`StaticNames`: raft's static mode, `reNoSnap =
  false`, leader transfer on, no snapshot directory, `reSnapOkRaw = sokOf snapOk`, `reCertNs = N`):
  `cluster_alloc` (bootstrapped, `StartNode`) and `cluster_alloc_static` (empty, `RestartNode`) both
  give `isStaticCluster γ N vs snapOk`, `leaderTransferOn` and the read credits. Every node takes a
  `MsgSnap` (`snapIn`; `NodeOk`). A client that wants no snapshot picks `snapOk := fun _ _ => False`.
- **Snapshots' certificates.** `snapshotCert` is raft's configuration certificate and the data's over a
  committed log the client knows (`isCommittedLogLb`), so `snapshotCert_data`/`snapshotCert_static` are
  plain entailments; it converts to and from raft's `raftSnapCertD` within `N`. `storageCertLink` is
  the two wands of the draft; it gives raft's `storCertOk` because raft's certificate namespace
  (`RaftNames.reCertNs`, new: commit `e63dee0352`, as `reNs` for the commit invariant) is the
  cluster's whole `N` (the conversion opens the adapter's invariant, inside `N`). A `MemoryStorage`'s
  registry (`storageCertInv`) is at `N .@ "cert"`.
- **`readyRecv`**: the loop's new state stated, by a `match` on the `Ready`'s snapshot loan: `delivered ++
  ce`, or the committed log up to the snapshot (`strip l.dlv`); the hard state `phsNext st.hardState h`;
  busy with `(es, L)`. `readyRest`/`readySnap` take `es h L`. The snapshot case is proved
  (`node_ready_receive`, `readySnapData`; the certificate from the storage's link).
- **Changed statements** (all proved): `readStateOk_ctx` (an update within `N`, given a committed lower
  bound at least `idx` long, `▷ ▷`); `cluster_alloc` (`|={E}=>`, the receipts' bound, `ps ≠ []`, `0 ∉
  ps`, `bootMarshal`, `snapOk`; out: read credits, `isStaticCluster`, `leaderTransferOn`; `nodeBoot γ N
  ps ctxs id`); `cluster_alloc_static` (+ read credits); `StartNode` (`storageCertLink`, not `storCap`);
  `node.Advance` (no premise on conf-change entries: raft's static mode needs none);
  `readyRecv`/`readyRest`/`readySnap` (above); `isStaticCluster_normal` removed (false: a client may
  propose conf changes, which commit). New: `readCredits` (+ `_split`, `readCredit_eq`),
  `node.ApplyConfChange.spec` (static: `CCShrink` of the voters, the voters' `ConfState` back).
- **Not done: `isStaticCluster_filler_normal`** (every committed filler of a static cluster is
  normal). Not provable from the trust base: `ccDecodeV2` is opaque, so an empty `ConfChangeV2`
  (bytes `[]`) a client proposes may, for all the proof knows, decode to a change with changes, which
  the leader accepts outside a joint configuration (`raft.go:1335`) and which then commits as a type-2
  filler. Proving it needs both protobuf's fact that `[]` decodes to the empty message (a trust-base
  change, the user's decision) and a static-mode record of `stepLeader`'s choice on the log's entries
  (`StepC.propose` allows any `PropRepl` replacement today). kv needs no such law: it applies only
  normal entries and type-1 conf changes.
- Raft: the allocation's continuation learns `reNs`, `reCertNs` and the boot registrations. Trust base
  unchanged (13 axioms, 0 sorries).

## Proposals keyed by type and data; fillers only fire `noopAu` (2026-10-27, branch `raft-api`)

For the node API redesign (`Proof/go_etcd_io/raft/v3/NodeApiDraft.lean`), where the client gives an
update only for entries it requested, raft's proof now tracks every entry but a **filler** as a
proposal:

- **Fillers.** `Filler ty d`: `d = []`, of type normal (`0`) or `ConfChangeV2` (`2`)
  (`Protocol/Ghost.lean`). `propDataIs γ e none` is `Filler ∧ CCDecodes`. The decoding conjunct is
  needed by `propData_ccEnts`; `ccDecodeV2` is opaque, so an empty `ConfChangeV2` is not known to
  decode. Only fillers fire the standing `noopAu`.
- **Keys.** The registry's key is `entKey ty d = u32Le ty ++ d`, which is injective (`entKey_inj`).
  `propDataIs γ e (some k)` is `entKey e.Type' e.Data' = k ∧ ¬Filler ∧ CCDecodes`, with
  `deposited γ k`. `entTk` is the key's ticket for a non-filler. Every non-filler is tracked:
  normal entries with bytes, conf changes, the bootstrap entries.
- **The bootstrap entries** are registered at allocation (`boot_register`, `Protocol/Facts.lean`):
  - Each is a proposal with the trivial result predicate and one deposit, already appended at its
    index.
  - The client gets the fresh-token authority at `bootFresh L` (`allocClientGen`,
    `allocClientBoot`).
  - `BootWf L` (no `ccOk` any more) asks for no filler and distinct keys. `BootLogOk ps bootLog`
    (no `ccOk`) gives them with `ps.Nodup`, a new premise of `ownRaftGhost_alloc_boot`.
- **Specs:**
  - `node.Propose`: `⌜data = []⌝ ∨ propArg γ (entKey (W32 0) data) Q`; the old `data ≠ []` is gone.
  - `node.ProposeConfChange`, `RawNode.ProposeConfChange`: `ccPropArg γ o` (`ApiVocab`) replaces
    `CCAllowed`. Once `o` is marshaled to `bs`, a `={⊤}=∗` step gives either `Filler` or `propIs ∗
    propAu1` for `entKey ty bs`. It is deposited by `cc_propose_ghost`. A refused change's ticket is
    dropped, and its update never fires.
  - `RawNode.Propose` lost its `data ≠ []`.
- **`reCCOk` is unused.** It is still a `RaftNames` field set by the allocation. Removing it would
  ripple through the allocation statements and the clients.
- **Clients (kv, etcd server) are not updated.** They are expected to break on this branch:
  `CCAllowed`, `BootLogOk`'s arity, `allocClient*`'s `bootFresh`, and `propArg`'s key.

## Raft's signature, stage 1: the node API (2026-10-26, branch `raft-modsig`)

`notes/decisions.md`, "Package signatures, enforced by Lean's module system". In short:

- **What a client sees:** `Spec/go_etcd_io/raft/v3/Api.lean` is what a client of raft imports.
  The API modules `InvNode` and `InvNodeCtx` import raft's internals non-publicly.
- **What is sealed:** the node's channel and ghost machinery is `@[no_expose]`: `isNode`,
  `nodeDriver`, `nodeDriverBusy`, `readyP`, the channel protocols, `nodeCfg` and `dlvLb`. Raft's
  own proofs `import all InvNode`.
- **Where the vocabulary went:** what the API's statements use moved out of the internals into
  `ApiVocab`. `Linked` (`RaftLink`) re-exports the linked results that proofs outside the linking
  files use.
- **New laws, replacing the clients' unfolds:** `isNode_id`, `isNode_commitInv`,
  `nodeDriver_isNode`, `readyP_take(_ns)`. The server's `rn_ready_recv` no longer re-derives
  raft's ghost step.
- **Checked:** (then `etc/sig-check.py`; now `etc/api-check.py etc/api/raft.txt --check`) no module outside raft
  reaches `InvRawnode`, `InvRawnodeReady`, `InvRawnodeC`, `InvNodeRun`, `InvBoot` or `InvRaftPhys`
  (1099 did before). Its 20 warnings are other packages' non-linking modules that import a linking
  file.
- **Then (2026-10-26, the user's choice):** an importable list per package (`etc/api/raft.txt`,
  `etc/api-check.py`, replacing `sig-check`) and a generated interface of the listed modules
  (`etc/gen-interface.py`, `interface/`), with layout checks; the class prototype removed
  (`notes/decisions.md`, "Package APIs").
- **Unchanged:** no statement and no trust base.
- **Open:**
  - The protocol and `Storage`/`MemoryStorage` vocabulary is still transparent.
  - `NodeNames` is still a structure.
  - The `RawNode` specs are outside the signature.
  - The linking-file imports above.

## Review of raft's public specs (2026-10-26, branch `worktree-raft-spec-review`)

`notes/raft-spec-review.md` has the findings, and its second part a modularity review: nothing but `ownRaftPhys` is sealed; the Storage contract carries raft's proof protocol (it changed at about ten stages, each re-opening the storage instances); the server and kv unfold `isNode`/`nodeDriver`/`netP`/`fwdP`, re-proving the Ready receive and the message hand-off. In short:

- **Raft's specs:** no raft spec is wrong or vacuous. The raft collection rests on 13 axioms and
  no `sorry`. `isCommitted_agree`, the proposal tickets and `readStateOk` give agreement,
  at-most-once updates and linearizable reads.
- **Open, high: `rnStopOkStarted` is false in the model.** It is the server examples' premise
  (`NodeBridge.lean:111`), and `isNode` gives `stop` the payload `False`, so no `Stop` step can
  keep the handshake invariant. `putget_safe` and the other closed theorems that take it through
  `Hprem` are therefore vacuous. D19r (A) restated the old premise for the same reason. Fixing it
  is a decision on a trusted statement: prove `node.Stop` (a stoppable node model) or make
  `onStop` unreachable and drop the clause.
- **Open, medium:**
  - No current theorem shows that a bare `MemoryStorage` meets the `Storage` contract, which the
    server's premises need (deleted in `9bfc967717`).
  - The server's `□` `InitialState` closure cannot be derived from `MemoryStorage.InitialState`'s
    spec (suspected).
  - `RawNode.Step` takes no `MsgProp`.
  - Nine `RawNode` specs are used by no proof.
  - No restart from persisted state.
- **Low:** a list of headers whose prose has drifted from the statements.
- **Filed:** `issues/raft-compact-past-snapshot.md`, with a reproduction.

## The client's KV specs over etcd's whole KV state; the libraries over them (2026-10-26, branch `worktree-kv-stated-specs`)

`notes/decisions.md` D44 (one stated gRPC spec per KV method, the client's `kv.Put`/`Get`/`Delete`/
`Do` and `txn.Commit` over one cluster-level `isKv kv γ dup` with the caller's atomic update written
in the spec, `□?dup`), D45 (no workload: the client spec supports what the proof supports; a
client's own facts in its invariant; no built-in restriction on the raft log), D46 (the state
multi-revision), D47 (`KVState ⟨compacted, base, changes⟩`: each revision's changes, in order; a
watch as repeated reads of the state) and D48 (the clients' model of etcd an adapter over the KV
state; the replies say their state is a well-formed small log's).

- The server, the client library (`KVService`, the specs, `Results`), the cache, recipes,
  concurrency, leasing, kubernetes, k8s's etcd3 store and every example build. `SrvWorkload`,
  `KVNames.wl`, the `writes` predicate, `srvNoDupKeys` and the examples' workloads are gone.
- `watcher.Watch.spec` is the watch as repeated reads of the KV state (`watchStateElem`: each
  response one firing of the caller's read update, its events exactly the state's range events,
  a progress notification at or past the position, which moves to it), proved over the client
  watcher's pipeline (the positions' facts `posQ`, `cur2Places`).
- The KV replies say their state is a well-formed small log's (`kvLogOk`, a write's state after
  too; a moving watch response `kvLogOkTo` through the new position), from the receipts' bound in
  `isKv` and `srvKVFacts`.
- The clients' model of etcd is an adapter over the KV state (`client/v3/EtcdModelKV.lean`,
  `etcdModelOfKV γ`, invariant `kmInv`, with an application's property of the changes `γ.W`), and
  the libraries' contracts are proved from the public specs at it: `KMGet` (`isEtcdKVE`,
  `isEtcdKVTodo`: linearizable gets only), `KMPut` (`isEtcdPutKVTodo`, with `kmPutRestTodo` for the
  puts the spec cannot serve: leased ones, and `IgnoreValue`/`IgnoreLease` ones of an absent key,
  which `kv.Put.spec` lets succeed without writing although the server answers `ErrKeyNotFound`:
  stating in `putStOk` that a successful put wrote would leave only the leased ones;
  `isEtcdDeleteKVTodo`, with `kmReachedAt γ 1`), `KMTxn` (`isEtcdTxnKVTodo`, with `kmReachedAt γ 1`
  and `kmTxnUncoveredTodo`: serializable read-only transactions, leased or `IgnoreValue` writes),
  `KMWatch` (`isEtcdWatcher`, `isEtcdProgressNotifier`), `KMClient` (`isEtcdClient`,
  `isKv_of_regs`). The cache's end-to-end results (`cache_end_to_end_client`, `_new`) and the
  recipes' (`queue_vertical`, `isEtcdRecipesClient_of_km`) are over the adapter; watchkv, cachekv
  and linkv3p's `MainWatch` keep their plan's fact in `γ.W`.
- Open: the recipes' range watcher (`isEtcdRangeWatcher`, single-key watches) is a premise: the
  Watch spec covers prefix watches only; generalizing it is about half a day (`cplCond`,
  `covers_prefix`), then the header's ownership, `rev = 0` and the cursor on progress (one to two
  days). STM's serializable reads cannot be connected through the adapter (a serializable read
  fires no update). The server-model bridges that no result uses any more (`ServerKV*`'s server
  theorems, `v3rpc.etcdModelOfServer`'s client-side uses, `InvServerKV`) are left for a clean-up.

## The server's token facts (E2c) (2026-10-25, branch `auth-e2c`)

The auth plan's E2c (`notes/auth-plan.md`; `notes/decisions.md`, "E2c of the auth plan"): the
server-side facts E2b found `Main` needs.

- **The context's own token**: `AuthInfoFromCtx`'s auth info is `nil` or bound to the token the
  request context's incoming metadata carries (`auth.ctxTokenOf ctx`, over the opaque
  `metadata.incomingOf`; `FromIncomingContext`'s trust-boundary spec and `rpctypes`' token-key
  initializers say more, same axioms). `ctxBound`, `ctxBoundOrTLS`, `principalBound`,
  `principalBoundI`, `adminOutB`, `authedOutB` and the guards' bound variants take the context.
- **One user per token** (`tokIssued_agree`): `tokIssued` keyed by the token, issuing spends the
  exclusive right (`tokFresh`), the authority keeps each issued token's spent right.
- **The simple shape** (`tokIssued_shape`): every issued token is `<prefix>.<raft index>`; the bad
  token was issued to no one (`tokIssued_badToken`, `authkv_badToken_not_issued`).
- Trust base unchanged (718 axioms, 5 sorries).

## The end-to-end auth example (E2b) (2026-10-25, branch `auth-e2b`)

The auth plan's E2b (`notes/auth-plan.md`; `notes/decisions.md`, "E2b of the auth plan").

- **The program** `examples/authkv` (project `authkv`): one member with the simple token
  provider, auth set up and enabled through a client (`SetUp`), four principals (`u` with role
  `r` on `[a, b)`, `v` with none, no token, the token `badtoken`) running puts, ranges, deletes,
  transactions (both branches, nested) and watches inside and outside `[a, b)`; `Main` panics if
  a refused request returned no error, a reply holds a key its principal may not read, or root's
  watch of the history shows a write its principal was not permitted. Go test passes, also under
  `-race`; translated; its `Init`/`PkgTable` generated.
- **Proved**: `InRange`, `Permitted` (`Link.lean`) and, pure, the model's verdict at the
  set-up's state (`Model.lean`'s `setupSt`, `granted_setupSt_iff`) and the bad token's shape
  (`ClientAuth.lean`); restated in `Results.lean`, collection `etc/tcb-collections/authkv.txt`.
- **Stated, not proved**: `Main`'s triple (`Spec/.../authkv/Main.lean`; the proof a `sorry`, +1
  to the baseline), with watchkv's premises for the server's start.
- **Found**: `ctxBound` must name the context's token (a bad principal's request was bound to
  "some issued token"); the issued tokens' shape and one user per token are needed facts (all
  three done in E2c);
  D29's refusal-freedom is false of an auth-enabled member (the bad principal's writes are
  refused with a refusal and resent by the client). Each is in the decision, with the client's
  auth contract C1-C4.
- **E2f (2026-10-26)**: the checks proved and linked (`keyOf`, `refused`, `Principals`, `Writer`,
  `LastIn`, `CheckHistory`, `checkKVs`, `checkTxnReads`); the contract C1-C4 over the contexts'
  metadata (`ClientAuth.lean`, `grpc/metadata/Outgoing.lean`; C3 the trust-boundary spec
  `metadata.AppendToOutgoingContext`, +1 axiom), `reqCtx` proved, `badCtx_unbound`. Left:
  `SetUp` (the client's `Auth` field and the server's Auth service unspecified), `Work`, `Main`
  (the server in the mode `on`), and that the timeout context carries no outgoing token

## The watch shapes (A4) (2026-10-24, branch `auth-a4`, worktree `/shared/etcd-grove-a4`)

The auth plan's A4 (`notes/auth-plan.md`; `notes/decisions.md`, "A4 of the auth plan").

- **The statement**: a created, not canceled, control response's watcher (`v3rpc.ctrlWatcher`,
  in the stream specification `watchDn`) carries `v3rpc.watchAuthed γ c`: in some mode the
  store's owner tag names (`auth.modeTag γ.tag M`; the server's, `watchSrvOk`), the class of the
  request's read for some principal (`apply.watchClass M info c.key c.rangeEnd`, the key
  normalized -- empty is `"\x00"` -- and the range end as the request gave it, the check's
  arguments) and the request's shape (`auth.reqShape`). `recvLoop` keeps `isWatchPermitted`'s
  class (A1's) and builds it at the registration.
- **The bridge to mvcc's range** (`v3rpc/WatchClass.lean`): `createRangeOk_inRange`, every key
  the registered `mvcc.WatchRange` covers is in the model's interval of the check, for a point,
  a proper range, `"\x00"` (`WithFromKey`: the rewritten end `[]`, or `none` in the model) and the
  empty key; `watch_permitted_covers`; `ctrlWatcher_authorized`, restated as `Results.lean`'s
  `watch_registered_authorized`: in `on γa`, a recorded state at which auth was disabled, or the
  principal a root user, or one whose READ permissions cover every covered key. GHSA-xg4h-6gfc-h4m8
  (the check after the rewrite of `"\x00"` to `[]byte{}`, a point check for an open-ended watch) is
  what this lemma excludes at the pinned revision.
- **The mode's name**: the stream specification (`watchDn γs γ cid mid j m`) has no auth mode in
  scope and its arity is fixed by the client's proofs and the examples; the mode is recorded
  under a ghost name of the watchable store's names (`mvcc.WsNames.tag`, the owner's tag:
  `newWatchableStore`/`mvcc.New` take it as `γtag`, of no meaning to mvcc), tagged by
  `server_kv_watchable_of` with the server's mode (`.off` in `NewServer`), exported by
  `srvWatchBuilt`/`srvWatchReaders` and held by `watchSrvOk`.
- **Progress/cancel requests** register nothing (`ctrlWatcher` is `True` of them); `Fragment` and
  the filters change no class. The principal is per create request (`AuthInfoFromCtx` of the
  stream's context, S5's binding): a watcher registered under a token later revoked keeps
  delivering, as etcd documents.
- Trust base unchanged; no closed theorem's statement changed (the examples run in `off`).

## The checks compute the verdicts (S3) (2026-10-24, branch `auth-s3`, worktree `/shared/etcd-grove-s3`)

The auth plan's S3 (`notes/auth-plan.md`; `notes/decisions.md`, "S3 of the auth plan").

- **The verdict's shape corrected** (`auth/Model.lean`): A0's `permVerdict` promised one recorded
  state at which `permitted` (with the revision conjunct) held on a pass and one at which it failed
  on a refusal; neither is true of `isOpPermitted`, which reads the flag, the revision, the user and
  the cache under four locks (an admin change between the revision read and the user read defeats
  the first; a missing user is read at another state than the flag for the second). Now `permitted
  st ai key rangeEnd op := st.enabled = false ∨ granted st ai key rangeEnd op` (no revision), and
  the `on γa` verdict is: a state that permitted and a state whose revision admitted the token (or
  at which auth was disabled) on a pass, a view of the four states read (`AuthView`, `recordedV`)
  in which the check refuses (`refusedV`) on a refusal; `adminVerdict`'s refusal names the flag's
  and the user's states (`adminRefused`). `reqShape` (a non-empty key; a point, an open-ended or a
  proper range: what the cache decides) is a premise inside `granted`/`refusedV`. `authStateAt`/
  `authHist` carry `permKeysOk`. A1's `classOk` and A2's `adminRes` consume the unchanged first
  conjunct.
- **The invariant** (`auth/InvAuth.lean`): `enabledP st M q` and `revInv st M` hold the mode's
  verdict beside the flag and the atomic; `enabledRd st M`, `authRd`, `authInv` thread the mode;
  `authInfoAt a dq ai` (`Option AuthInfo`: `nil` or the message).
- **The specs** (`Spec/.../auth/`): `isOpPermitted` for an `AuthInfo` whose fields are the
  arguments, returning `permVerdict M info k e (permOp pt) err`; the three `Is*Permitted`
  `permVerdict` with their type; `IsAdminPermitted` over `authInfoAt` returning `adminVerdict M ai
  err`; `IsAuthEnabled` `enabledVerdict`, `Revision` `revisionVerdict`; `hasRootRole`'s axiom
  restated (a sorted-roles message, `decide (isRoot ur.roles)`, the message kept). Proved by
  `auth/VerdictLemmas.lean` (one lemma per branch of the Go code, for every mode).
- **The contract** (`apply/Contracts.lean`, `apply/AuthDerive.lean`, `etcdserver/AuthGuard.lean`):
  `isAuthStore` gains `IsAdminPermitted(nil)` as its last clause (A2's premise `adminNilOk`/
  `srvAdminNilOk` is derivable: `adminNilOk_of_isAuthStore`, `srvAdminNilOk_of_srvAuthAt`;
  dropping it from the 12 guarded entry points' specs is a mechanical follow-up);
  `isAuthStore_of_authInv` derives the contract in the store's own mode (was `.any`).

## Kubernetes' etcd3 storage backend: phase 4's unary methods proved (2026-10-22, branch `k8s-etcd3`)

**2026-10-23: merged into `lean`.** The merge ported the work to lean's changes: the driver's
`Main` starts its member through the shared start (`common.StartServer`, `common.Serve`, D33; a
write sent at most once because the member is refusal-free, D29, so `kubernetes.New`'s spec no
longer gives a one-attempt fact), the kubernetes client's proofs read `clientErr`/`statusErrOk`
out of D37's `kvErr` and use `ClientPutGet.lean`'s lemmas (D35), linkv's modules come from
linkvtxn (D34), and the etcd pin is `goose-lean-getproph2` (`bc9c3868c`). `k8setcd3_safe` and its
four `sorry`s unchanged; D37 discharges the sentinel half of `clientErr_other` only (plan, item 5).

**2026-10-23: the driver's closed theorem** (stage 6g of `notes/k8s-etcd3-plan.md`).
`k8setcd3_safe` (`Proof/github_com/mit_pdos/etcd_grove/examples/k8setcd3/Results.lean`): one
in-process member, the kubernetes client, the seeded store, the etcd3 store over it and porcupine's
check of `Create`/`Get`/`Delete`/`GuaranteedUpdate` traffic against the driver's model never panic
or get stuck, and return `Ok` or `Unknown`. Its hypotheses are linkvtxn's at the driver's
configuration, the Kubernetes packages' semantics assumptions and `objTyOk` (a method-set fact).
It rests on four `sorry`s: `revRoom` (the revision bound, D30n), `clientErr_other` and
`client_ctx_field` (from the client proof's owner: items 5 and 6 of the plan), and `kvIs_ne_null`
(item 3). **2026-10-26: `clientErr_other` proved** (D37b in `notes/decisions.md`): the client's
error is no sentinel (D37's `errCellOk`, carried by the kubernetes client's and the store's error
cases, against the sentinels' message cells in the driver's package fact), a pointer if an
`*errorString` (`errCellOk_ptr`), and no `*StorageError` (a leaf, and `*StorageError` has
`Unwrap`: the new method-set premise `storageErrTyOk` of `k8setcd3_safe`); three `sorry`s left. The trust base adds the trust-boundary axioms of the names-only functions on the
initialization and constructor paths (`etc/tcb-collections/k8setcd3.txt`); Perennial limitations
found: `≤u` without a transitive instance, embedded interfaces' type sets, `os.Getenv`/
`strconv.ParseBool` (`notes/perennial-changes.md`).

`notes/k8s-etcd3-plan.md` (decisions D30a-l; D30h-j and D30l proposed). Branch `k8s-etcd3`: `lean` with the
translation survey `k8s-etcd3-goose` merged; merged into `lean` 2026-10-23, the etcd pin moved
to the fork's `goose-lean-getproph2` (`bc9c3868c`: `goose-lean`'s `188113160` with the prophetic
`kubernetes.Client.Get`).

- **A finding**: `correctness.Model` rejects the store's intended rewrite of non-canonical or stale
  data on a no-op update (`issues/k8s-correctness-model-noop-rewrite.md`, Go reproduction). D30g
  (decided): the generic specs use a model with a canonical bit per item; the driver keeps its
  non-canonical codec and checks against a fixed copy of the Model in `examples/k8setcd3/`.
- **The model** (`Proof/k8s_io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/Model.lean`, sorry-free): `create`,
  `delete`, `update`, `get` over linkv's abstraction (D30i), `correctness.Model`'s update on
  canonical states; the store's transactions move it as the model (`absK_create`, `absK_delete`,
  `absK_update`), keeping the store's states (`KWf_put`, `KWf_del`).
- **The object contract** (`Contract.lean`, D30k): the codec, versioner, transformer and decoder
  as a premise (`contractOk`), the WPs of the exact calls the store makes (`runtime.Encode(codec,
  obj)` among them), errors with an `Error()`.
- **The kubernetes client** (`Spec`/`Proof/go_etcd_io/etcd/client/v3/kubernetes/`, linked):
  `Get`, `OptimisticPut`, `OptimisticDelete` over linkvtxn's failover calls (`Calls.lean` now
  needs only the client's and v3rpc's assumptions). Their errors are the client's (`clientErr`,
  `statusErrOk`: the failover lemmas `client_*_any` and `txn_Commit_st` now keep them). One
  `sorry`, `kvIs_ne_null`: a response's key-value pointer is not `nil`, which `txn.kvIs` does not
  state (the plan's request 3 to the client proof). `Count` not done.
- **The store** (`Proof/k8s_io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/`, linked by `etc/gen-link.py
  --k8s-etcd3`; collection `etc/tcb-collections/k8s.txt`):
  - `store.Get`: a linearizable read (the caller's persistent read update at each member, whose
    state is the store's): the model's `get` at the state it fired at (`respIs`: the object at
    its mod revision, the zero object, "not found"), or the client's error.
  - `store.Create`: a write fired at most once (`k8sAu1`, D30h's one-shot part: the caller's
    relational update, whose next state the store chooses; `k8sAu1_kvAu1` turns it into the
    client's for the transaction it sends, by `stepOk_create`): the model's `create` at the state
    it fired at (the object at the new revision, or "key exists", `create_out`), or an error.
  - Helpers: `prepareKey`, `storage.PrepareKey` (against `prepareKeyM`), `getTypeName`,
    `txnError`, `validateMinimumResourceVersion` (no minimum), the storage error constructors.
  - Restrictions for now: a valid key, no minimum resource version on `Get`, an input object
    without a resource version on `Create`, `ttl = 0`.
- **Trust base added**: trust-boundary axioms for the names-only calls of the unary paths
  (tracing `Start`/`AddEvent`/`End`, `audit.GetAuditIDTruncated`, the store's metrics,
  `strings.HasSuffix`/`Contains`, `reflect.TypeOf`); the package facts in
  `Proof/k8s_io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/Base.lean` (`True`, but the metrics package's
  `ErrTransactionConflict`).

- **`store.Delete`** (linked; D30l: the caller's persistent read-or-write update `k8sAuRW` with
  a write token `W`): its outcome is the model's `delete` (`delOut`): at the state the write fired
  at, the deleted object at the new revision; or at the read a read-like answer came from ("not
  found", `validateDeletion`'s error, nothing changed, `W` back); or the client's error. The
  pieces, each proved and linked: `stateFromEtcdResponse` (the store's reading of a key-value into
  a fresh object of the store's type, through `reflect`), `getCurrentState` (a persistent closure,
  `getStateOk`), `refreshOnError` (a current state), `deleteOnce` (`OptimisticDelete` from the
  caller's updates, `k8sAusRW_kvAu1`; a key-value at the read mod revision has the read value by
  the caller's history, `kvSeen_same`, D30j; success is the model's `delete`, `delete_at`; a
  conflict leaves etcd's state as it was, `del_cases`), `conditionalDelete` (the retry loop).
  Restrictions for now: a valid key, no preconditions, no cached object, no unsafe deletion of a
  malformed object (`opts.ExpectTransformOrDecodeError` false); `validateDeletion` is the caller's
  callback answering a function of the object (`validateOk`).
- **`store.GuaranteedUpdate`** (linked; D30l's update with the model's `update`): its outcome is
  the model's `update` with the canonical bit (`updOut`): the write at the state it fired at
  (`destination` the result at the new revision); a read-like answer at a read (`tryUpdate`'s
  error, "not found", or the no-op of an unchanged canonical object: the store's
  `!stale && bytes.Equal(data, origState.data)` is the model's test, `update_skip` by
  `noop_iff`); or an error (the client's, the codec's, the transformer's). `tryUpdate` is the
  caller's callback answering a function of the object and its revision (`tryUpdateOk`,
  persistent: it runs at each retry, D30h's "repeatable spec"). The pieces: `updateState`,
  `updateOnce` (as `deleteOnce`, by `put_cases`/`update_at`/`updStepOk`),
  `storage.Preconditions.Check` on `nil`; `refreshOnError` now on `ownStateX` (the state without
  its object, which `tryUpdate` took). Restrictions for now: a valid key, `ignoreNotFound` false,
  no preconditions, no cached object, no TTL.
- **The caller's updates, reworked for the driver's linearization points (D30n, 2026-10-23)**:
  `k8sAuRW` (`Updates.lean`) no longer has a read postcondition `Q` and a write token returned at
  reads: it fires as a plain read any number of times, and once as the linearization point, which
  hands the caller's timeless token `W` (the model's `step` must hold there: the write, or, at a
  read, a state where the step is the identity, `stepHand`). The first read goes through a call
  invariant (`FirstRead.lean`, `rwInv`): `Client.Get` is now prophetic (the etcd fork's branch
  `goose-lean-getproph`, `942601555`, off the pinned `2aed163b1`: `Get` resolves a prophecy of the
  response's revision and the key's mod revision, so its spec's single read update fires at the
  state with that pair), and `rwInv_after` gives the caller's result at a state with the answer's
  item and revision (`update_local`/`delete_local`) or `W` back. `deleteOnce`/`updateOnce` hand the
  result at a conflict whose state is the identity; `conditionalDelete`/`GuaranteedUpdate` carry it
  in their loops. The outcome predicates (`delOut`, `updOut`) are two cases: the client's error, or
  the caller's result at a state with the model's answer. All proved and linked; the trust base is
  unchanged.
- **The driver's linearization (stage 6f, 2026-10-23)**: `examples/k8setcd3`'s `Apply` proved
  logically atomic against the driver's model (`k8setcd3S g0`) in `lintest`'s `applySpec` form:
  the invariant (`Proof/.../k8setcd3/Inv.lean`), the updates and commits (`InvSteps.lean`),
  `errOut`, `call`, `Apply`. Two marked `sorry`s (D30n): etcd's revisions do not run out
  (`revRoom`), a client error is neither a `*StorageError` nor the driver's sentinels
  (`clientErr_other`). The store's `Get` is now prophetic (a read update per prophesied pair) and
  the caller's write updates report `KvNext` (`Updates.lean`); the store's history authority is
  `History.lean`. Not yet linked: 6e and 6g remain.
- The contract now names the objects' Go type (`ObjSpec.objTy`: a non-nil pointer to it,
  `objAt_ptr`; `reflect.New`'s allocation is the zero object, `newObj`; a `runtime.Object` and not
  a `runtime.Unstructured`, `tyOk` in `contractOk`).
- `reflect`'s reasoning principles, as axioms for now (the user's choice, 2026-10-22; a trusted
  model with proved principles later, in Perennial): `Proof/reflect/Values.lean` (`reflect.Value`'s
  typed points-to, `reflElem`/`reflPtr`/`reflType`/`reflNew`) and the specs of `reflect.New`,

- More trust base: `klog.V`/`Verbose.Infof` (axioms, now linked); `util/feature`'s package fact

## The examples' clients configured as in practice: request timeouts (2026-10-23, branch `client-timeouts`, worktree `/shared/etcd-grove-ct`)

`notes/client-timeouts-plan.md` (T0, T1 and T2's gates done; T3 waits on Perennial),
`notes/decisions.md` D-T1..D-T5. The etcd examples' clients made every call with
`context.Background()` and set no `DialTimeout`; keepalive was linkv3p's alone. Now:

- **The configuration** (`examples/common/common.go`): etcdctl's defaults, `DialTimeout` 2s,
  `RequestTimeout` 5s, `KeepAliveTime` 2s (grpc's 10s floor applies), `KeepAliveTimeout` 6s;
  `common.NewClients(eps, lg)` (`NewClient(addr, lg)` is `NewClients({addr}, lg)`); linkv3p's
  `newClient` (10s / 2s) is gone. Every member's `common.Serve` passes embed's keepalive policy
  (`MinTime` 5s), as linkv3p's `startMember` did.
- **Every unary call** in `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(),
  common.RequestTimeout)`, `cancel()` after the call (client/v3's documented form): putget's and
  putget3's Put and Get, `common.Writer`, linkv3p's `writer`, linkvtxn's five `call*`. Watches keep
  `WithCancel`.
- **The proofs.** One lemma, `client.wp_WithTimeout_bg`
  (`Proof/go_etcd_io/etcd/client/v3/TimeoutCtx.lean`), over the read loop's trust-boundary axiom
  `context.WithTimeoutBackground` and `context.ErrAny`: the context is `ctxOk` and `ctxErrClient`
  (`ctxErrClientAllW_of`'s argument, under `ContextReadErrs` and `ContextErrsClient`), `cancel`
  callable. Each call site applies it, calls at the new context, and `cancel`'s triple; every
  spec on the call chains takes the two classes. `common.NewClients` is linkv3p's `newClient`
  spec and proof moved (`clientCfgOk` leaves `DialTimeout` free, keepalive by `kaOpts`).
- **Statements.** The conclusions of the closed theorems are unchanged; `putget_safe`,
  `putget3_safe`, `linkvtxn_safe` and `linkv3p_safe` take `ContextErrsClient` (the watch theorems
  did), since a timed-out call's error now flows through the client.
- **Trust base.** No new axiom (the baseline stays at 539); `grpc.KeepaliveEnforcementPolicy.wp_proof` enters the
  `putget`, `putget3`, `linkvtxn`, `watchkv` and `cachekv` collections (+1 each).
- **The Go tests.** All pass (`go test` of every example, linkv3p with `-race`). linkv3p's
  `TestFailover` rewritten: the blackholed member's calls fail at 5s, 10s and 15s (request
  timeouts, reads too: the client never retries past the caller's deadline) until the keepalive
  close at 16s fails the calls in flight; then failover and the return. `cutRun` accepts a read
  that failed at its request timeout and no other read failure; `TestWatchFailover`'s blackholes
  are 18s (past the 16s close). `TestFailover` takes about two minutes (12000 operations per
  worker).
- **T3 (branch `with-timeout-bg`, the same day).** Perennial `c25bef57e` (branch
  `with-timeout-background`): `wp_WithDeadlineCause_Background_of`, `wp_WithDeadline_Background_of`,
  `wp_WithTimeout_Background_of` (`Proof/context/WithDeadlineBackground.lean`: the no-deadline
  branch of `WithDeadlineCause`'s proof over `Background()`'s facts), exposed in its `Results`;
  `propagateCancel`'s spec takes any child for a `Background()` parent (Go never looks at the
